claim: When GnT1IP-L is overexpressed, Golgi-localized MGAT1 is markedly relocated to the ER.

claim: Transfection of Iv/GnT1IP-L-Myc into HeLa cells gave predominant expression in the ER.

claim: Co-transfected MGAT1-HA was largely localized to the Golgi compartment in HeLa cells expressing Iv/GnT1IP-L-Myc.
source: Transfection of Iv/GnT1IP-L-Myc into HeLa cells gave predominant expression in the ER, whereas co-transfected MGAT1-HA was largely localized to the Golgi compartment (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding shown in Figure 5A.

claim: Expression of Iv/GnT1IP-L-Myc in wild type CHO cells was robust.
source: Expression in wild type CHO cells was robust but did not lead to resistance to L-PHA when either Iv/GnT1IP-L-Myc or Iv/GnT1IP-L-Myc-KDEL were overexpressed in CHO cells (Figure 5B,C).

claim: Expression of Iv/GnT1IP-L-Myc in wild type CHO cells did not lead to resistance to L-PHA.
source: Expression in wild type CHO cells was robust but did not lead to resistance to L-PHA when either Iv/GnT1IP-L-Myc or Iv/GnT1IP-L-Myc-KDEL were overexpressed in CHO cells (Figure 5B,C).

claim: Expression of Iv/GnT1IP-L-Myc-KDEL in wild type CHO cells did not lead to resistance to L-PHA.
source: Expression in wild type CHO cells was robust but did not lead to resistance to L-PHA when either Iv/GnT1IP-L-Myc or Iv/GnT1IP-L-Myc-KDEL were overexpressed in CHO cells (Figure 5B,C).

claim: GnT1IP-L that is largely localized to the ER does not inhibit MGAT1 activity.

claim: MGAT1 and MGAT2 undergo homomeric interactions in the ER.

claim: MGAT1 and MGAT2 undergo heteromeric interactions in the Golgi.

evidence: This is a statement about previous findings supported by citations.

claim: Nocodazole treatment caused GnT1IP-L-VN and GnT1IP-L-VC to accumulate in the ER.

claim: A BiFC signal was observed indicating GnT1IP-L homomer formation in the ER after nocodazole treatment.
source: A BiFC signal was observed indicating GnT1IP-L homomer formation (Figure 6A, Nocodazole).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding shown in Figure 6A.

claim: In the absence of nocodazole, GnT1IP-L homomers were transported to the Golgi.
source: In the absence of nocodazole (Control), homomers were transported to the Golgi.
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding shown in Figure 6A.

claim: When GnT1IP-L–VN was co-transfected with MGAT1-VC, a BiFC signal was not detected in nocodazole-treated cells.
source: By contrast, when GnT1IP-L–VN was co-transfected with MGAT1-VC, a BiFC signal was not detected in nocodazole-treated cells (Figure 6B), indicating that heteromer formation did not take place in the ER (Figure 6B).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding shown in Figure 6B.

claim: Heteromer formation between GnT1IP-L and MGAT1 did not take place in the ER.
source: By contrast, when GnT1IP-L–VN was co-transfected with MGAT1-VC, a BiFC signal was not detected in nocodazole-treated cells (Figure 6B), indicating that heteromer formation did not take place in the ER (Figure 6B).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the BiFC data in Figure 6B.

claim: In the absence of nocodazole, GnT1IP-L-VN and MGAT1-VC were transported to the Golgi with the concomitant emergence of the BiFC signal due to heteromer formation.

evidence: This is a primary experimental finding shown in Figure 6B.

claim: Nocodazole treatment relocated Golgi-localized heteromers of GnT1IP-L and MGAT1 to the ER.

claim: Nocodazole treatment caused a concomitant reduction of the FRET signal between GnT1IP-L and MGAT1.

claim: Removal of nocodazole allowed reformation of heteromeric complexes between GnT1IP-L and MGAT1 in the Golgi.

claim: GnT1IP-L homomers were not affected by nocodazole treatment.

claim: Increasing the pH of the Golgi by approximately 0.4 units following incubation for 4–16 hr in chloroquine inhibits heteromer formation between glycosyltransferases.
source: Previous experiments showed that increasing the pH of the Golgi by ∼0.4 units following incubation for 4–16 hr in chloroquine inhibits heteromer formation and favors homomer formation between glycosyltransferases (Hassinen and Kellokumpu, 2014).
evidence: This is a statement about previous findings supported by citation.

claim: Increasing the pH of the Golgi by approximately 0.4 units following incubation for 4–16 hr in chloroquine favors homomer formation between glycosyltransferases.
source: Previous experiments showed that increasing the pH of the Golgi by ∼0.4 units following incubation for 4–16 hr in chloroquine inhibits heteromer formation and favors homomer formation between glycosyltransferases (Hassinen and Kellokumpu, 2014).
evidence: This is a statement about previous findings supported by citation.

claim: Treatment with chloroquine for 4 hr did not significantly reduce GnT1IP-L homomers.
source: Compared to untreated controls, either treatment with chloroquine did not significantly reduce GnT1IP-L homomers, but caused an ∼60% reduction in GnT1IP-L/MGAT1 heteromers (Figure 8A and Figure 8—source data 1).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding shown in Figure 8A.

claim: Treatment with chloroquine for 16 hr did not significantly reduce GnT1IP-L homomers.
source: Compared to untreated controls, either treatment with chloroquine did not significantly reduce GnT1IP-L homomers, but caused an ∼60% reduction in GnT1IP-L/MGAT1 heteromers (Figure 8A and Figure 8—source data 1).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding shown in Figure 8A.

claim: Treatment with chloroquine for 4 hr caused an approximately 60% reduction in GnT1IP-L/MGAT1 heteromers.
source: Compared to untreated controls, either treatment with chloroquine did not significantly reduce GnT1IP-L homomers, but caused an ∼60% reduction in GnT1IP-L/MGAT1 heteromers (Figure 8A and Figure 8—source data 1).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding shown in Figure 8A.

claim: Treatment with chloroquine for 16 hr caused an approximately 60% reduction in GnT1IP-L/MGAT1 heteromers.
source: Compared to untreated controls, either treatment with chloroquine did not significantly reduce GnT1IP-L homomers, but caused an ∼60% reduction in GnT1IP-L/MGAT1 heteromers (Figure 8A and Figure 8—source data 1).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding shown in Figure 8A.

claim: The proportion of GnT1IP-L homomers increased almost twofold after 16 hr chloroquine treatment, presumably due to the disruption of heteromer formation.
source: The proportion of homomers increased almost twofold, presumably due to the disruption of heteromer formation (16 hr treatment), or their disassembly (4 hr treatment) at the higher Golgi pH (Figure 8B and Figure 8—source data 1).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding shown in Figure 8B with interpretation.

claim: Chloroquine treatment did not impair the Golgi localization of any of the test proteins.
source: Chloroquine treatment did not impair the Golgi localization of any of the test proteins (Figure 8C).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding shown in Figure 8C.

claim: GnT1IP-L forms homomers in the ER.
source: Therefore GnT1IP-L, like MGAT1 as shown previously (Hassinen and Kellokumpu, 2014), forms homomers in the ER and heteromers with MGAT1 in the acidic Golgi lumen, where it inhibits MGAT1 activity.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the FRET and BiFC experiments.

claim: GnT1IP-L forms heteromers with MGAT1 in the acidic Golgi lumen.
source: Therefore GnT1IP-L, like MGAT1 as shown previously (Hassinen and Kellokumpu, 2014), forms homomers in the ER and heteromers with MGAT1 in the acidic Golgi lumen, where it inhibits MGAT1 activity.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the FRET and BiFC experiments.

claim: GnT1IP-L inhibits MGAT1 activity in the acidic Golgi lumen.
source: Therefore GnT1IP-L, like MGAT1 as shown previously (Hassinen and Kellokumpu, 2014), forms homomers in the ER and heteromers with MGAT1 in the acidic Golgi lumen, where it inhibits MGAT1 activity.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the combined experimental data.

claim: GL54D is the most abundant species amongst membrane proteins in rat testis Golgi preparations.
source: A recent study of rat testis identified GL54D, the rat homologue of mouse GnT1IP-S, as the most abundant species amongst membrane proteins in Golgi preparations (Au et al., 2015).
evidence: This is a statement about previous findings supported by citation.

claim: Rat GL54D is confined to spermatocytes and spermatids.
source: Immunohistochemistry showed that rat GL54D is confined to spermatocytes and spermatids, consistent with the expression pattern of GnT1IP transcripts in purified mouse germ cells (Figure 9; [Soumillon et al., 2013a]).

claim: GnT1IP-S is secreted from CHO cells.
source: Thus, while the GL54D homologue GnT1IP-S is secreted from CHO cells (Huang and Stanley, 2010), it is likely to be membrane-bound in mouse germ cells, similar to GL54D in rat (Au et al., 2015).
evidence: This is a statement about previous findings supported by citation.

claim: GnT1IP-S is likely to be membrane-bound in mouse germ cells.
source: Thus, while the GL54D homologue GnT1IP-S is secreted from CHO cells (Huang and Stanley, 2010), it is likely to be membrane-bound in mouse germ cells, similar to GL54D in rat (Au et al., 2015).
evidence: This is an inference based on homology and citation.

claim: No complex N-glycans that might reflect GlcNAc transfer were identified by mass spectrometry in CHO N-glycans generated following expression of membrane-bound GnT1IP.
source: In characterizing the CHO N-glycans generated following expression of membrane-bound GnT1IP, no complex N-glycans that might reflect GlcNAc transfer were identified by mass spectrometry, but rather a great increase in the abundance of the Man5GlcNAc2 substrate of MGAT1 was observed (Huang and Stanley, 2010).
evidence: This is a statement about previous findings supported by citation.

claim: A great increase in the abundance of the Man5GlcNAc2 substrate of MGAT1 was observed in CHO N-glycans generated following expression of membrane-bound GnT1IP.
source: In characterizing the CHO N-glycans generated following expression of membrane-bound GnT1IP, no complex N-glycans that might reflect GlcNAc transfer were identified by mass spectrometry, but rather a great increase in the abundance of the Man5GlcNAc2 substrate of MGAT1 was observed (Huang and Stanley, 2010).
evidence: This is a statement about previous findings supported by citation.

claim: GnT1IP-L induces increased binding of GNA in a variety of cell lines including CHO, COS-7, HeLa cells and PC3 cells.
source: In addition, we have shown that GnT1IP-L induces increased binding of GNA reflecting enhanced expression of oligomannose N-glycans, increased resistance to lectins that bind complex N-glycans, and/or inhibition of MGAT1 activity, in a variety of cell lines including CHO, COS-7, HeLa cells (Huang and Stanley, 2010; this work) and PC3 cells (unpublished observations).
evidence: This is a statement about experimental findings from previous and current work.

claim: GnT1IP-L induces increased resistance to lectins that bind complex N-glycans in a variety of cell lines.
source: In addition, we have shown that GnT1IP-L induces increased binding of GNA reflecting enhanced expression of oligomannose N-glycans, increased resistance to lectins that bind complex N-glycans, and/or inhibition of MGAT1 activity, in a variety of cell lines including CHO, COS-7, HeLa cells (Huang and Stanley, 2010; this work) and PC3 cells (unpublished observations).
evidence: This is a statement about experimental findings from previous and current work.

claim: C1GALT1C1 is a specific chaperone dedicated to the Gal-transferase C1GALT1.
source: Importantly however, another example of a gene that has homology to, and the protein domain structure of a glycosyltransferase, but an activity that is distinct, is C1GALT1C1, originally called COSMC (Ju and Cummings, 2002; Wang et al., 2010). This protein is a specific chaperone dedicated to the Gal-transferase C1GALT1, and essential for its activity (Wang et al., 2010).

claim: C1GALT1C1 is essential for C1GALT1 activity.
source: This protein is a specific chaperone dedicated to the Gal-transferase C1GALT1, and essential for its activity (Wang et al., 2010).

claim: The only activity yet identified for membrane-bound GnT1IP is as a specific inhibitor of MGAT1.
source: Thus, although GnT1IP-L (or MGAT4D) has homology to family 54 glycosyltransferases, the only activity yet identified for membrane-bound GnT1IP is as a specific inhibitor of MGAT1.
evidence: This is a summary statement about the current state of knowledge.

claim: The gene encoding GnT1IP-L is most highly expressed in testis compared to other mouse tissues.
source: A functional role for GnT1IP-L has been proposed in testis based on the following: the gene encoding GnT1IP-L is most highly expressed in testis compared to other mouse tissues (Wu et al., 2009, 2013; Djureinovic et al., 2014; Fagerberg et al., 2014), the expression of the transcript encoding GnT1IP-L is developmentally regulated (Huang and Stanley, 2010); GnT1IP is well expressed in spermatocytes and spermatids but not in spermatogonia (Chalmel et al., 2007; Huang and Stanley, 2010); and cells expressing GnT1IP-L and oligomannose N-glycans bind more tightly to TM4 Sertoli cells than cells expressing MGAT1 and complex N-glycans (Huang and Stanley, 2010).
evidence: This is a statement supported by multiple citations.

claim: The expression of the transcript encoding GnT1IP-L is developmentally regulated.
source: A functional role for GnT1IP-L has been proposed in testis based on the following: the gene encoding GnT1IP-L is most highly expressed in testis compared to other mouse tissues (Wu et al., 2009, 2013; Djureinovic et al., 2014; Fagerberg et al., 2014), the expression of the transcript encoding GnT1IP-L is developmentally regulated (Huang and Stanley, 2010); GnT1IP is well expressed in spermatocytes and spermatids but not in spermatogonia (Chalmel et al., 2007; Huang and Stanley, 2010); and cells expressing GnT1IP-L and oligomannose N-glycans bind more tightly to TM4 Sertoli cells than cells expressing MGAT1 and complex N-glycans (Huang and Stanley, 2010).
evidence: This is a statement supported by citation.

claim: GnT1IP is well expressed in spermatocytes and spermatids but not in spermatogonia.
source: A functional role for GnT1IP-L has been proposed in testis based on the following: the gene encoding GnT1IP-L is most highly expressed in testis compared to other mouse tissues (Wu et al., 2009, 2013; Djureinovic et al., 2014; Fagerberg et al., 2014), the expression of the transcript encoding GnT1IP-L is developmentally regulated (Huang and Stanley, 2010); GnT1IP is well expressed in spermatocytes and spermatids but not in spermatogonia (Chalmel et al., 2007; Huang and Stanley, 2010); and cells expressing GnT1IP-L and oligomannose N-glycans bind more tightly to TM4 Sertoli cells than cells expressing MGAT1 and complex N-glycans (Huang and Stanley, 2010).
evidence: This is a statement supported by citations.

claim: Cells expressing GnT1IP-L and oligomannose N-glycans bind more tightly to TM4 Sertoli cells than cells expressing MGAT1 and complex N-glycans.

claim: Conditional deletion of the Mgat1 gene in spermatogonia blocks spermatogenesis in mice.

claim: GnT1IP/Mgat4D is exclusively expressed in post-meiotic germ cells in mouse.

claim: Mgat1 is expressed at lower levels in all germ cell types in mouse.

claim: Antibodies to rat GnT1IP (GL54D) detect signals in spermatocytes and spermatids but not spermatogonia.

claim: The GnT1IP/Mgat4d gene undergoes post-meiotic transcriptional activation.

claim: GnT1IP/MGAT4D is very highly expressed in human testis compared to 26 other tissues examined by RNA-Seq.

claim: MGAT4D transcripts are highly enriched in human testis (29 FPKM compared to a maximum FPKM of 0.1 for MGAT4D transcripts in 26 human tissues).

claim: GnT1IP/MGAT4D transcripts are very poorly expressed in testicular phenotypes with only pre-meiotic germ cells (only spermatogonia present).

claim: MGAT1 has highest expression in testicular phenotypes without germ cells (TA, SCO).

claim: MGAT1 expression is largely restricted to testicular somatic cell types in humans.
